c7a14df35c.q: What is the strategic framework for becoming bookable on national television?
c7a14df35c.a: Jamie developed a framework called KNOWN to help people become bookable and produce themselves. K stands for know your message, which requires clarity so a producer can sell you to their team and communicate the value you will offer. The framework emphasizes that getting booked is strategic and requires thinking through who you are, who you serve, and the expertise you bring.
c7a14df35c.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

aec31c70a4.q: How do media producers decide which guests get pitched to their editorial team?
aec31c70a4.a: When a producer is lining a show and mapping out the outline, an executive producer determines what guests go in those spots. At pitch meetings, teams of potentially 20 people come to the table with two or three guest ideas and angles, and they need to be able to sell you as the right fit for that show and audience.
aec31c70a4.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

c20b54096f.q: What makes a pitch relevant to a television news outlet or media network?
c20b54096f.a: You need relevance on two fronts: the news cycle and the network's current needs. For example, if a show has a cooking segment coming up around Memorial Day, a cookbook author should pitch a barbecue idea. You want to be thinking about where your audience is in that moment in time as well as the news cycle, and providing the media with a creative way to serve their audience.
c20b54096f.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

44c387be65.q: How should aspiring media guests build a credible trail to attract producer interest?
44c387be65.a: You should focus on getting quoted as an expert in published articles first. When you have a trail of support like being quoted in Forbes magazine or other publications, producers can tell their teams about you and it helps position you as an expert worth considering. Your online audit should help you figure out where you are, what you have, and what you need to build that credibility trail.
44c387be65.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

251d5ec73b.q: Why is response speed critical when media producers reach out to potential guests?
251d5ec73b.a: Media producers work around the clock and search for experts at odd times of day. If they find you and reach out, how quickly you respond will increase your chances of getting booked. When a producer says 'can you come tomorrow?' you need to be ready immediately, because the opportunity moves fast.
251d5ec73b.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

66a2f16dff.q: What role does your online presence play in a media producer's decision to book you?
66a2f16dff.a: Your online presence is your pre-interview. Producers will look at your social media, blog posts, YouTube videos, and LinkedIn activity to decide if they want to reach out to you. If you are not showing up and strategically positioning yourself across the internet, it is really hard for producers to justify booking you, because they cannot assess how you will perform on camera.
66a2f16dff.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

d13ff4df84.q: How can experts build media relationships before they need publicity for a book launch?
d13ff4df84.a: You should start building relationships well in advance of a book launch by providing value to the media outlet's audience without making an ask. Rather than pitching 'I have a book, can I come on?', you should show up as an expert in your industry willing to talk about stories that need coverage. Build relationships because you don't need anything right now, showing up well before you need the attention.
d13ff4df84.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

d21b88d9f1.q: What common mistake do people make when pitching to the wrong media outlets?
d21b88d9f1.a: You don't want to be pitching the wrong sources. If you are pitching a legal show, for example, do not pitch a hot dog eating contest. You need to make sure that you are aligned with the outlet and that you are pitching in a way that makes sense to their audience and editorial focus. Study what a show actually covers before sending your pitch.
d21b88d9f1.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

1b19124613.q: How can experts use social media to attract media attention without traditional PR outreach?
1b19124613.a: You can comment on articles or topics of interest on Twitter or LinkedIn with your own expert point of view, without chasing press. The media will find you because you are showing up deliberately commenting on something in the press with your own platform. Nina Jankiewicz got op-ed opportunities from the Wall Street Journal by writing on Twitter about her expertise in disinformation, without ever pitching—the media came to her.
1b19124613.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

b4c441c079.q: What is the value of owning and sharing your personal story to attract media opportunities?
b4c441c079.a: The vulnerability you share now could be the value add later, and the messy middle is worth sometimes sharing. Kendall Williams built an Instagram account of over 100,000 followers by talking about being estranged from her son—a topic few people were discussing on social media. Because of her authentic storytelling, Oprah's producer reached out, she appeared on Oprah, which led to the Wall Street Journal writing about her, which led to USA Today coverage and speaking engagements.
b4c441c079.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

739b03eff9.q: How should you pitch a product or concept with visual elements to television producers?
739b03eff9.a: You need to think about how your expertise could be presented visually, create a headline, and provide them with visuals in the pitch itself. For example, when pitching a product that turns air into water, creating a video to include in the pitch helped it gain traction with Fox and Friends. Data is also a great way to get booked on TV because it automatically presents the opportunity to be displayed visually.
739b03eff9.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

80154899e7.q: What type of research study is most credible for media pitching purposes?
80154899e7.a: Online studies are not as strong to the media as backed studies. Studies need to be backed by credible institutions or researchers to carry weight in media pitches. A Ph.D.-led study is stronger than an independent online survey when pitching to television producers.
80154899e7.e: Jamie Maglietta: How to Get Booked on TV

5fe04db4ca.q: How does a CEO's personal brand impact the company's ability to recruit top talent and close deals faster?
5fe04db4ca.a: Executives with strong personal brands are reported to close deals faster and attract several times more qualified job candidates. The personal brand of a CEO shapes who walks through the door, who stays, and who believes in where the company is going. When candidates already follow the CEO's podcast, audiobook, or social media, they come pre-aligned with company values, which significantly shortens the recruiting cycle and reduces vetting time.
5fe04db4ca.e: Why Your Personal Brand Matters More When You're the CEO

b73365efd3.q: What is the quantified relationship between CEO reputation and overall company reputation according to research?
b73365efd3.a: A 2026 research study from Deloitte found that nearly half of a company's reputation is determined by the reputation of the leader. This finding underscores that the personal brand and reputation of the person in charge shapes the entire company's future, including the ability to recruit, attract, and retain top performing team members.
b73365efd3.e: Why Your Personal Brand Matters More When You're the CEO

827387ef38.q: How should CEOs approach talent acquisition differently from traditional job postings?
827387ef38.a: Instead of posting a standard job description, the CEO should write recruitment sales letters that sell a vision of who the company is and its culture. This approach represents the CEO's personal brand voice and communicates mission-driven purpose before candidates apply. Candidates should feel like they are joining a movement or a mission, not just filling a job role.
827387ef38.e: Why Your Personal Brand Matters More When You're the CEO

21ca3176b2.q: What are the four core responsibilities a CEO should prioritize once a business reaches stability?
21ca3176b2.a: The four core CEO functions AJ Vaden identified are: chief talent acquisition officer, chief vision officer, chief culture protector, and implicitly maintaining financial and operational oversight. She emphasized that these priorities shift once the business moves past startup mode and achieves stability in position, people, process, and finances.
21ca3176b2.e: Why Your Personal Brand Matters More When You're the CEO

2b038ef68b.q: How does dreaming big as a CEO directly influence team performance and culture?
2b038ef68b.a: According to the principle that 'your people will do half of what you do right and twice of what you do wrong,' the CEO must dream twice as big as team members to inspire them toward ambitious goals. When the CEO embraces seemingly impossible visions, team members come alive with new ideas, initiative, and creative problem-solving. This big vision thinking forces leaders and their teams to think differently and activate dormant capabilities.
2b038ef68b.e: Why Your Personal Brand Matters More When You're the CEO

09cfd30864.q: How does being transparent about leadership philosophy through personal branding help with culture alignment?
09cfd30864.a: When a CEO is clear and unapologetic about their values, beliefs, and leadership philosophies—whether about sales, revenue generation, or decision-making—team members know exactly where they stand and can opt in or opt out accordingly. This transparency helps filter for culture fit and allows team members to understand the reasoning behind tough decisions, building trust and alignment within the organization.
09cfd30864.e: Why Your Personal Brand Matters More When You're the CEO
